before_behavior: Step 1 of each wave: 'Before any work, snapshot the current project state. Write to .wabblespec/checkpoints/wave-<N>-<timestamp>/. Record: wave number, timestamp, list of files that will be touched by this wave. This snapshot is the rollback target. The checkpoint must exist before Guard runs.' authority.owns in skill-rules.json includes '.wabblespec/checkpoints/*'.
after_behavior: Step 1 of each wave is eliminated. The rollback ground truth is the locked wave plan at .wabblespec/plans/current-wave-plan.md, which already declares outputs and files touched by each wave. SKILL.md step 1 becomes: 'Rollback reference: the locked wave plan is the ground truth for this wave. If this wave must be rolled back, revert all files listed under this wave in current-wave-plan.md to their pre-wave state. No pre-wave directory snapshot is written.' The post-wave session checkpoint at .wabblespec/session/checkpoints/checkpoint-wave-<N>.json (step 5b) is unchanged. authority.owns in skill-rules.json removes '.wabblespec/checkpoints/*' and retains '.wabblespec/session/checkpoints/*'.

benchmark_gates.rationale: A rollback intervention rate above 10% (more than 1 in 10 sessions requiring manual recovery after wave failure) indicates the pre-wave directory checkpoint was providing real recovery value. In the current corpus of 33 executor activations, 0 rollback interventions occurred — confirming the pre-wave checkpoint was never used. The 10% threshold gives a 3x safety margin over the 0% base rate.

fixture_spec.developer_scenario: A wave fails mid-implementation with no pre-wave directory checkpoint available. Recovery uses the locked wave plan to identify which files were touched and reverts them.

notes: Secondary change: skill-rules.json authority.owns must remove .wabblespec/checkpoints/* once pre-wave writes are eliminated. guard-check.py authority tests must be updated accordingly. Both files are in scope for Augment.
